extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rulewriters, administrative lawyers, and regulated or interested members of the public (notice-and-comment participants)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory procedural requirements for informal notice-and-comment rulemaking under 5 U.S.C. §553, including what notice must say, who must be given notice, exceptions, opportunities for participation, timing of publication, and petition rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / scope exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies, according to the provisions thereof, except to the extent that there is involved- (1) a military or foreign affairs function of the United States; or (2) a matter relating to agency management or personnel or to public property, loans, grants, benefits, or contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies categories of governmental action to which §553 does not apply; use to determine whether the rulemaking procedures in §553 are triggered.

rubrics_metrics.name: General notice publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: General notice of proposed rule making shall be published in the Federal Register, unless persons subject thereto are named and either personally served or otherwise have actual notice thereof in accordance with law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default requirement: publish proposed rules in the Federal Register. An alternative is individual notice where affected persons are named and personally served or have actual legal notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must state time, place, and nature of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall include a statement of the time, place, and nature of public rule making proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement ensures interested persons know when/how to participate; applies to public rulemaking proceedings (e.g., public meetings/hearings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must reference legal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall include reference to the legal authority under which the rule is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must cite the statutory or other authority supporting the proposed rule so commenters can assess legal basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must provide terms or substance (or description) of proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall include either the terms or substance of the proposed rule or a description of the subjects and issues involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be sufficiently specific: either publish the proposed regulatory text or describe the subjects/issues so that interested parties can comment intelligently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must give internet address of plain-language summary (≤100 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall include the Internet address of a summary of not more than 100 words in length of the proposed rule, in plain language, that shall be posted on the Internet website under section 206(d) of the E-Government Act of 2002 (commonly known as regulations.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a short, plain-language summary posted online (regs.gov) and the address referenced in the Federal Register notice; added by Pub. L. 118–9 (2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories exempted from notice/hearing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when notice or hearing required by statute, this subsection does not apply- (A) to interpretative rules, general statements of policy, or rules of agency organization, procedure, or practice;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretative rules, policy statements, and organizational/procedural/practice rules are excluded from the notice-and-comment requirements of subsection (b) unless another statute requires notice/hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-cause exception to notice/hearing (with required findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when notice or hearing required by statute, this subsection does not apply... (B) when the agency for good cause finds (and incorporates the finding and a brief statement of reasons therefor in the rules issued) that notice and public procedure thereon are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency may bypass notice-and-comment by making and publishing a 'good cause' finding and brief reasons in the final rule; the acceptable justifications are impracticability, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to participate (written and oral submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice required by this section, the agency shall give interested persons an opportunity to participate in the rule making through submission of written data, views, or arguments with or without opportunity for oral presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must permit interested persons to submit written comments; agencies may also allow oral presentations (e.g., hearings), but oral presentations are not always required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to incorporate concise general statement of basis and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: After consideration of the relevant matter presented, the agency shall incorporate in the rules adopted a concise general statement of their basis and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules must include a brief statement explaining the agency's basis and purpose, showing consideration of public input and rationale for choices made.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-record hearings: sections 556 and 557 applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: When rules are required by statute to be made on the record after opportunity for an agency hearing, sections 556 and 557 of this title apply instead of this subsection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another statute mandates trial-like on-the-record proceedings, the formal hearing/adjudicative procedures of §§556–557 replace the informal procedures in §553(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of effective date: 30-day publication/service requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The required publication or service of a substantive rule shall be made not less than 30 days before its effective date,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, substantive rules cannot take effect until at least 30 days after publication/service to allow regulated parties time to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to 30-day effective-date requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The 30-day requirement does not apply to: (1) a substantive rule which grants or recognizes an exemption or relieves a restriction; (2) interpretative rules and statements of policy; or (3) as otherwise provided by the agency for good cause found and published with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the situations where an agency may make a rule effective sooner than 30 days, including agency-published good-cause findings (which must be published with the rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition for issuance, amendment, or repeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall give an interested person the right to petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide a petition process allowing interested persons to request new rules or changes to existing rules.
